_about: Expected readings of statblock_formats.md (ROADMAP #74, Phase 1): every accepted stat block format, most common first, and the model each must read into.

The model: {name, meta, fields: [{label, value}], scores: [{name, score, mod, save}], sections: [{name, entries: [text]}]}. Entries before the first section heading go in a section named ''. Text keeps its inline markup as written (bold/italic markers are not part of the model's labels and names). mod and save use a true minus sign. save is '' unless the format gives one. Whether a modifier was written or worked out is not part of the model, so a format that writes them and one that doesn't read the same.

Formats 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b and 3 must read into exactly the same model, 'bog_thrall_classic', except that 1b has no markup to keep (its entries are compared with markup stripped). Format 4 reads into 'bog_thrall_2024'; format 5 into 'marsh_ghoul_osr'.

The source is stored as written: a stat block is a line-oriented fence, so the Markdown round trip keeps every line in whatever format it was pasted. Only the reading is normalised, and so only the printed result looks the same.

rank.name: Classic 5e layout, bold labels with no colon
rank.why: How 5e homebrew is typed in Word and Google Docs, and what copying from D&D Beyond gives; the author's own Bestiary is written this way.

rank.name: Classic layout pasted from a PDF, no formatting
rank.why: Copying a stat block out of any PDF; the commonest way a block arrives without markup.

rank.name: Homebrewery V3 ({{monster}} with :: fields)
rank.why: The most used free tool for DMs Guild homebrew; V3 is its current renderer.

rank.name: Homebrewery legacy / GM Binder (___ and > lines)
rank.why: A large back catalogue of homebrew is in this form, and GM Binder still uses it.

rank.name: Colon form (Label: value)
rank.why: Forums, Reddit, plain-text notes; the app's own native form.

rank.name: 2024 5e layout
rank.why: The current edition's books and the SRD 5.2 (CC-BY-4.0) use it; newer homebrew follows.

rank.name: Old-school one-line stat line
rank.why: OSR games (Old-School Essentials, B/X clones) write a creature as one line of abbreviations.

reading_rules: Fence attributes win: name= and meta= on the fence line are the name and meta; otherwise the first line is the name (with any ** or ## removed) and the next line is the meta if it is italic or, unformatted, begins with a size (Tiny, Small, Medium, Large, Huge, Gargantuan).

Wrapper lines are ignored: a line that is only ___ or ---- style rules (three or more underscores), '{{monster' and its options, '}}', a lone ':', and a lone '>' or a blank line. A leading '> ' and a leading '- ' list bullet are stripped from every line first.

A field is any of: 'Label: value'; '**Label** value'; '**Label:** value'; '**Label** :: value'; or, with no markup, a known label at the start of the line followed by its value. Known labels: Armor Class, AC, Hit Points, HP, Speed, Initiative, Saving Throws, Skills, Damage Vulnerabilities, Damage Resistances, Damage Immunities, Vulnerabilities, Resistances, Immunities, Condition Immunities, Gear, Senses, Languages, Challenge, CR, Proficiency Bonus.
A line with two or more bold labels is that many fields ('**AC** 9    **Initiative** −1 (9)').

A line of two or more '|'-separated pieces that are each 'Label: value' is that many fields ('Combat: 45 | Instinct: 60 | Armor: 10'); if any piece is not, the line is one field ('Speed: 30 ft. | climb 20 ft.').

Unformatted known labels are only read as fields in the head: the head ends after the Challenge, CR or Proficiency Bonus line, or at the first section heading, so a trait called 'Speed Demon.' after them is an entry.

Scores, in any of these shapes, consecutive lines merged into one row: 'STR 14 | DEX 8 | …'; 'STR 14 (+2) DEX 8 (−1) …' with no pipes; a line of names then a line of values ('STR DEX CON INT WIS CHA' / '14 (+2) 8 (−1) …'); a Markdown table of names, an alignment row and values; the 2024 'Str 14 +2 +2' (score, modifier, save), in rows of three or six. Names in capitals or title case (Str or STR), never lower case. Modifiers are worked out only for the six 5e names.

A section heading is any of: '--- Name'; '### Name' or '## Name' after the name line; a line that is only bold ('**Actions**'); or, unformatted, a line that is only a known section name. Known section names: Traits, Actions, Bonus Actions, Reactions, Legendary Actions, Mythic Actions, Lair Actions, Regional Effects, Spellcasting.

An old-school stat line is one line of known abbreviations (AC, HD, Att, THAC0, MV, SV, ML, AL, XP, NA, TT, and also Move, Save, Morale, Attacks, No. Appearing, Treasure); it splits into fields at each comma or semicolon that is followed by one of them, so commas inside a value stay in it.

With no markup, an entry's name is a phrase of up to 6 words at the start of a line, in title case (every word capitalised except a, an, the, and, or, of, by, in, on, to, with, for), ending in a full stop (optionally after a parenthesis, as in 'Toll (Recharge 5–6).') and followed by more text; it is printed as the style prints entry names. A sentence in sentence case ('Drowned voices whisper from the walls. One creature…') is never a name. 'ft.' and other abbreviations inside a field value are not affected, since fields are read first.

expect.unfenced: Exactly two stat blocks found and wrapped in ~~~ statblock fences (one V3, one legacy), each reading as a shortened Bog-Thrall (Armor Class, Challenge, the score row, one action); the three paragraphs around them stay paragraphs.

decided: Homebrewery blocks ({{monster}} … }} and the legacy '___' + '> ##' form) are only wrapped in a fence by the paste and import converter; the parser never reads them outside a fence, since a '>' line or '___' rule in a novel must never become a stat block. (User, 2026-10-07.)
The 2024 layout's saving throws print as their own column, as the 2024 books do: the preset's 'scores' setting gains 'table-2024' beside 'row' and 'grid'. (User, 2026-10-07.)
Unformatted entry names (title case, ending in a full stop) are recognised, inside a stat block fence only. (User, 2026-10-07.)
